In 16 appearances with the Dodgers this season, Díaz has
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers on Friday activated Edwin Díaz off the injured list, with a week and a half remaining in the regular season to see if his slim chance of pitching his way onto the postseason roster comes to fruition.
Díaz, who signed a three-year contract with the Dodgers in December, struggled to open the season before undergoing arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow in April, which cost him three and a half months.
In 16 appearances with the Dodgers this season, Díaz has allowed runs in nine of them, with an 11.85 ERA, 6.37 xERA, 19 strikeouts and 10 walks in 13 2/3 innings. In nine games after returning from elbow surgery, Díaz had a 19.6-percent strikeout rate, down from 30.3 percent in seven games before surgery, and well below his 39.9-percent career strikeout rate through 2025.
The latest malady for Díaz was neck inflammation, sidelined since August 18. His rehab assignment with Oklahoma City didn't go well at all, throwing more balls than strikes in three of his five appearances, with six runs allowed in 4 1/3 innings, seven walks, and four strikeouts. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Thursday in Cincinnati that Díaz will need to throw more strikes, and quality ones at that, in order to be considered to pitch in October.
"Like anything, it should be a meritocracy. You have to earn the right of opportunities, and you've also got to perform. Eddie understands that," Roberts said, as shown on SportsNet LA. "Where we're at now, we need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That's what he's about."
Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, after fulfilling his role with aplomb on Thursday. Called up for a day, Knack tossed four scoreless innings in relief and earned the win in the Dodgers' division clincher in Cincinnati.
In Knack's three stints in the majors this year, he pitched in four of the eight games for which he was active, with a 3.86 ERA and 4.09 xERA in build relief, with eight strikeouts and two walks in his 11 2/3 innings, plus one save of 2 2/3 innings, the Dodgers' longest save of the season.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are giving Edwin Díaz one final chance to prove he belongs on the postseason roster.
On Friday, ahead of their series opener against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers have officially activated Díaz off the 15-day injured list. In order to make room on the active roster, right-hander Landon Knack was optioned.
Díaz joined the Dodgers this offseason on a three-year, $69 million deal to be the team's closer. He had a 10.50 ERA over six innings before going on the injured list and undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
Díaz made his long-awaited return in late July, and the Dodgers were hoping his early-season issues would be behind him.
Unfortunately, that wasn't the case.
The three-time All-Star had an even worse 12.91 ERA over 7.2 innings. He then went back on the IL — this time with a neck injury — and has been out for the last month.
Díaz struggled on his rehab assignment, and there were questions about whether the team would even give him another chance this season.
“He needs to pitch better. It hasn’t been good,” manager Dave Roberts said on Monday. “He’s going to pitch on Wednesday, and I guess we’ll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well."
He had a better rehab outing on Wednesday, pitching one scoreless inning. That was enough for the Dodgers to give him one more opportunity at the big league level.
It won't be as the team's closer, though.
What Will Edwin Diaz's Role Be For Dodgers?
The Dodgers will be using Díaz in low-leverage spots at first as they see if he can be an option for the postseason roster.
“I think like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also got to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now, we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Across Díaz's 16 appearances this season, he has a disastrous 11.85 ERA and four blown saves in 11 chances.
However, if he returns to form in time for the playoffs, all will be forgotten from his disappointing first season in LA.

Noah Camras graduated from the University of Southern California in 2022 with a B.A. in Journalism and a minor in sports media studies. He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts: “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”
El campocorto de los Dodgers coloca en perspectiva la participación de la novena en la postemporada por decimotercera vez en los últimos 14 años.
PUBLICIDAD
Cincinnati. Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Reds de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Doc and the boys are ready for October. pic.twitter.com/krnwXYR7ap
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.title: [Orange County Register] Alexander: Can the Dodgers overcome the curse of the big contracts?
item.dc:creator: Jim Alexander
item.description: The world according to Jim: • Would it drive fans in other cities even further out of their minds if the Dodgers wound up three-peating despite minimal contributions from their two big free-agent signings of last winter? … • Kyle Tucker (four years, $240 million all told, $55 million in 2026 including a $54 million signing bonus according to Cot’s Contracts), might be starting to wake up at the plate after struggling to justify that contract for the first six-plus months. In the past eight games
item.content:encoded:
The world according to Jim:
• Would it drive fans in other cities even further out of their minds if the Dodgers wound up three-peating despite minimal contributions from their two big free-agent signings of last winter? …
• Kyle Tucker (four years, $240 million all told, $55 million in 2026 including a $54 million signing bonus according to Cot’s Contracts), might be starting to wake up at the plate after struggling to justify that contract for the first six-plus months. In the past eight games going into Friday night’s series opener against the Giants, he has a slash line of .310/.566/.586 with five homers, 11 RBIs and 14 runs scored in 29 at-bats.
Then again, that has come exclusively against the Cincinnati and Miami pitching staffs. But Tucker’s contract hasn’t been totally sunk money in this first year. …
• Edwin Díaz, on the other hand, signed for three years, $69 million total, and $23 million this season including a $9 million signing bonus. As of now, that comes to $3.285 million per save. In fairness, he got the win in two of his four blown saves – three of which came in August, two in back-to-back appearances in Arizona – but he has hardly been what the Dodgers envisioned when they signed him.
And he has been active 45 of a possible 178 days this season. He spent all of May, June and most of July on the injured list after a procedure to remove “loose bodies” from his elbow, and went back on the IL on Aug. 18 with neck inflammation. He’s set to be activated Friday, but barring some absolutely lights-out performances over the next two weeks, it’ll be a stretch to imagine him being on the Dodgers’ initial postseason roster. …
• I’d like to be snarky here and suggest that this proves big free-agent signings by themselves don’t automatically lead to championships – but the Mets have already proven that. …
• It became official this week and probably shouldn’t be a surprise: The Kings appointed Drew Doughty as captain, succeeding the retired Anze Kopitar. Given what Doughty has devoted to this franchise in 18 seasons and 1,279 games, including L.A.’s first Stanley Cups in 2012 and 2014, it’s appropriate.
And, yes, we’re already speculating who will ultimately succeed Doughty, who turns 37 in December. Adrian Kempe, Artemi Panarin and Mikey Anderson will be the assistant captains this season … and my money’s on Mikey to eventually inherit the C on his sweater. …
• This week’s quiz: Doughty will be the Kings’ 15th captain dating to the franchise’s inception in 1967. How many of the other 14 can you name? Answer below.
• The Kings, incidentally, begin their preseason Saturday night at Ontario’s Toyota Arena against Las Vegas. Their farm club, the Ontario Reign, will be wearing purple and gold along with black this coming season. (And in an apparent nod to original Kings owner Jack Kent Cooke, who loved the color purple but hated the word and thus decreed that it officially be called Forum Blue, the Reign will label theirs as Inland Blue.)
Can we convince the big club to add those colors, too? …
• Quiz answer: Bob Wall, Larry Cahan, Bob Pulford (one season before he was named head coach in 1972), Terry Harper, Mike Murphy, Dave Lewis, Terry Ruskowski, Dave Taylor, Wayne Gretzky, Luc Robitaille (as an interim captain early in the 1992-93 season while Gretzky was laid up with a back injury), Rob Blake (who succeeded Gretzky after the Great One was traded to St. Louis Feb. 27, 1996), Mattias Norstrom, Dustin Brown and Kopitar. …
• Meanwhile, across the county line, Ducks general manager Pat Verbeek got Cutter Gauthier’s signature on the dotted line of a six-year, $81 million deal just three hours before a more restrictive collective bargaining agreement took effect at 9 p.m. Pacific time Wednesday night.
You think Verbeek is like many of us were in school – and as, indeed, some of us still are? It takes a hard deadline to get anything done. …
• No need to rehash what happened last weekend, but this needs to be said: ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe handled herself with far more grace than those misogynist creeps who felt compelled to weigh in, as well as the idiot who generated the disgusting fake video of Steve Sarkisian slapping Rowe (and all of those who laughed about it). May that cretin have his AI toys taken away.
I’m with Team Holly. And this is yet another reminder of the garbage that women in sports media generally have to endure for no reason other than their gender. …
• UCLA’s new athletics CEO, Tim Harris, posted a large, blue W this week when he announced students now can attend football and men’s and women’s basketball games for free. This is how you (a) amp up the atmosphere at home games and (b) promote the loyalty that turns alumni into supporters and donors.
Next suggestion: Convince a corporate donor to sponsor those rooter buses from Westwood to the Rose Bowl and make them free as well. …
• The Pro Football Hall of Fame is cutting the size of its voting panel by almost half, from 50 to 28. Meanwhile, 428 ballots were cast in baseball’s Hall of Fame election last year by voting members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (and yes, I am one). Additionally, football Hall of Fame selectors are sworn to secrecy while BBWAA voters are encouraged to show their work, and most of us do.
Is it any wonder, then, that the general public seems far more invested in who gets to Cooperstown every year than in who gets selected for the shrine in Canton? …
• The Awful Announcing platform had this headline the other day: “Has sports on streaming failed?” The reaction (overreaction?) was to the opening week NFL ratings, with NBC’s New England-Seattle game Wednesday drawing far better national ratings than Netflix’s Rams-49ers game from Melbourne the following night.
Hidden in those numbers is a simple truth: A network over-the-air broadcast will always do better because it is more accessible – especially for those who can’t or won’t pay for all the streaming services that televise sports.
And maybe this is the pertinent question: Is the league working for the streaming service, and if so shouldn’t it be the other way around? At the very least, teams and leagues should insist that the streamer’s telecast be shown in the competing teams’ markets on either their regular TV outlets or, as the NFL does, an over-the-air channel.
jalexander@scng.com

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers manager Dave Roberts makes Edwin Diaz decision
item.dc:creator: Matt Larter
item.description: The MLB postseason is approaching, and the Los Angeles Dodgers are preparing to welcome relief pitcher Edwin Diaz back from the injured list as they look to finalize their bullpen for another World Series run. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has confirmed that Diaz will be activated Friday ahead of the team's three-game weekend series against the San Francisco Giants. However, the veteran reliever will not immediately return to the high-leverage role he was expected to occupy when he signed with Lo
item.content:encoded:
The MLB postseason is approaching, and the Los Angeles Dodgers are preparing to welcome relief pitcher Edwin Diaz back from the injured list as they look to finalize their bullpen for another World Series run.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has confirmed that Diaz will be activated Friday ahead of the team's three-game weekend series against the San Francisco Giants. However, the veteran reliever will not immediately return to the high-leverage role he was expected to occupy when he signed with Los Angeles.
Diaz will have to earn high-leverage opportunities
Mar 31, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Edwin Diaz (3) throws against the Cleveland Guardians during the ninth inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images
Roberts said Diaz will initially be used in lower-leverage situations when he returns and will have to "earn" his way into higher-leverage spots. The approach gives the Dodgers an opportunity to gradually reintegrate the right-hander while evaluating his performance and health ahead of the postseason.
Diaz has been sidelined since mid-August with a neck injury. His current absence is the latest setback in a difficult first season with the Dodgers after the club signed him to a three-year, $69 million contract with the expectation that he would serve as its closer.
The 32-year-old has also dealt with an elbow issue this season, undergoing arthroscopic surgery in April to remove loose bodies from his right elbow.
MORE: Wilson Contreras is 'frustrated' & calls out Red Sox
Dodgers face decision ahead of postseason
Diaz's numbers have made his return particularly intriguing. He has appeared in just 13.2 innings this season and owns an 11.85 ERA and 2.56 WHIP. He has allowed 18 runs on 25 hits during that limited workload.
With the postseason approaching, the Dodgers appear unlikely to immediately hand the closer role back to Diaz. Instead, Roberts' comments suggest the veteran will need to demonstrate that he can consistently get outs before being trusted in the most important moments of games.
Still, having Diaz available gives Los Angeles another experienced arm to evaluate as the playoffs draw closer. The Dodgers enter the final stretch of the regular season in a comfortable position, sitting nine games ahead of the San Diego Padres in the National League Central with nine games remaining.
Diaz is expected to be active for Friday's series opener against the Giants, giving him an opportunity to begin working his way back into the Dodgers' bullpen plans.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Rival executive underscores why Edwin Diaz belongs nowhere near Dodgers and how to fix him
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo
item.description: It's no secret that Edwin Diaz has had a nightmare first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers. Diaz was brought in on a three-year, $69 million deal in the offseason to be an elite closer for the Dodgers, but things haven't gone according to plan. He got off to a rough start to the season before undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies from his elbow in late April. This knocked him out for a little over three months, but upon his return, Diaz's performance didn't improve. Just three weeks after
item.content:encoded:
It's no secret that Edwin Diaz has had a nightmare first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers. Diaz was brought in on a three-year, $69 million deal in the offseason to be an elite closer for the Dodgers, but things haven't gone according to plan.
He got off to a rough start to the season before undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies from his elbow in late April. This knocked him out for a little over three months, but upon his return, Diaz's performance didn't improve. Just three weeks after being activated, he landed back on the IL with neck inflammation on August 18.
On the season, Diaz has an abysmal 11.85 ERA and four blown saves in 11 chances across 13⅔ innings. He has also struggled on his most recent minor league rehab assignment, allowing five runs, three walks and a hit by pitch in just 0.2 innings two outings ago. As a result, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated that the team could leave Diaz off their postseason roster.
What has gone wrong for Dodgers' closer Edwin Diaz?
One National League executive who spoke with FanSided gave his take on Diaz. The NL executive believes Diaz's lower arm angle has impacted his stuff. Diaz's arm angle has dropped each year since 2022 when it was 23 degrees. It lowered to 20 degrees in 2024 to 19 degrees in 2025 to just 15 degrees this year. This is something Diaz and the Dodgers are actively working to fix.
Diaz's fastball velocity is also down this season. He's averaging 96.3 mph on his four seamer as opposed to 97.2 mph in 2025. Opponents are hitting .441 with a .735 slugging percentage against his fastball. His slider velocity is normal, but hitters have a .323 average with a .516 slugging percentage against it. Last season, batters hit .179 with a .269 slugging percentage versus Diaz's slider.
In addition to his lower arm slot, the executive thinks that Diaz's struggles may have become partly mental after the mechanical/stuff issues. The executive compared Diaz to Tanner Scott, who had a poor first season with the Dodgers last season, and believes an offseason reset might do the trick like it did with Scott.
Scott is not having a good September (7.71 ERA), but has bounced back this season overall to post a 2.87 ERA, 1.02 WHIP, 76 strikeouts and 22 saves in 59.2 innings. He will likely be the Dodgers' closer in the postseason unless Diaz somehow miraculously turns his campaign around -- and fast.
Given the injuries, mechanical woes and mental aspect that comes with all of this, it appears that 2026 will be a lost one for Diaz. The three-time All-Star and three-time Reliever of the Year, has had a disastrous year and the most realistic hope is that he can return to form in 2027.

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Dodgers share updated projection for Andy Pages' return from injured list
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are returning for their final homestand of the 2026 regular season as National League West champions and on the verge of getting reinforcements back from the injured list. Edwin Díaz is expected to be activated on Friday, and Andy Pages may not be far behind. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not specify a date for his All-Star outfielder but said Pages was “very likely” to return during the homestand. Pages has been on the injured list since Aug. 22 due to a left hand fra
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are returning for their final homestand of the 2026 regular season as National League West champions and on the verge of getting reinforcements back from the injured list.
Edwin Díaz is expected to be activated on Friday, and Andy Pages may not be far behind. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not specify a date for his All-Star outfielder but said Pages was “very likely” to return during the homestand.
Pages has been on the injured list since Aug. 22 due to a left hand fracture. He underwent a procedure that involved inserting a screw into his left hand to accelerate the recovery process without extending the recovery timeline.
Thus, the expectation remained Pages would be back with the Dodgers in four to five weeks from the time of suffering the injury. An additional note is that Pages will forego a rehab assignment prior to getting activated.
The 25-year-old has been swinging a bat over the past several days and took a step forward on Tuesday by hitting off a pitching machine. He then advanced to taking at-bats against the Trajekt machine.
Tommy Edman stepped up in place of Andy Pages
Alek Thomas initially received the bulk of starts in center field but was removed from the roster on Sept. 1 as part of multiple moves.
Since then Tommy Edman has been an effective replacement in center field, but getting Pages back lets the Dodgers get their best nine players in the lineup just in time for the postseason.
Edman’s ability to play all over the field has long been valued by the Dodgers. It was a strong motivation for his acquisition from the St. Louis Cardinals at the 2024 trade deadline and a subsequent contract extension that offseason.
But Edman’s versatility has been even more so valuable lately with Shohei Ohtani and Pages sidelined. Roberts lauded Edman for his ability to impact a game with his glove and bat.
The 31-year-old said he takes pride in doing his best to fill the void left by Pages’ absence.
Now with Pages on the verge of returning, the Dodgers will likely move Edman back to second base but also have the option of further leveraging his positional versatility if needed.

item.title: [El Fildeo] Edwin Díaz regresa a Dodgers y pone en duda el rol de cerrador en 2026
item.dc:creator: Mike
item.description: Edwin Díaz está de vuelta en el bullpen de los Dodgers y la noticia trae algo más que alivio: trae una pregunta que el equipo tendrá que responder antes del postemporada. El cerrador puertorriqueño, uno de los más dominantes del circuito cuando está encendido, regresa a Los Ángeles en septiembre de 2026, pero el rol de cerrador ya estaba repartido. Ahora el bullpen más profundo de la Liga Nacional tiene un problema de lujos: demasiado talento para una sola posición. El regreso que nadie sabe cóm
item.content:encoded:
Edwin Díaz está de vuelta en el bullpen de los Dodgers y la noticia trae algo más que alivio: trae una pregunta que el equipo tendrá que responder antes del postemporada. El cerrador puertorriqueño, uno de los más dominantes del circuito cuando está encendido, regresa a Los Ángeles en septiembre de 2026, pero el rol de cerrador ya estaba repartido. Ahora el bullpen más profundo de la Liga Nacional tiene un problema de lujos: demasiado talento para una sola posición.
El regreso que nadie sabe cómo acomodar
Díaz no llega como una pieza de relleno. Llega como el mismo pitcher que alguna vez fue el relevista más emocionante de las Grandes Ligas, el hombre de las trompetas, el que hacía temblar el Citi Field con su entrada. El problema es que los Dodgers construyeron su bullpen asumiendo que él no estaría, y lo hicieron bien. Demasiado bien.
La jerarquía en el cierre de Los Ángeles ya tenía dueño. [DATO PENDIENTE: nombre del cerrador titular de los Dodgers en la temporada 2026 y estadísticas de ERA/saves antes de la llegada de Díaz.] Meter a Díaz en esa ecuación no es sumarle un refuerzo al equipo; es pedirle a alguien que baje un escalón, y en béisbol, los cerradores no bajan escalones fácilmente. El ego va junto con el rol.
Lo que hace interesante la situación no es solo quién cierra, sino cómo responde Díaz. En sus mejores años con los Mets — antes de la lesión de rodilla en el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol 2023 y la reconstrucción que vino después — era el tipo de pitcher que define innings. Ahora firma con un equipo donde nadie lo esperaba para ser el número uno y tendrá que demostrar que puede funcionar en otro papel, o convencer a la dirección de que merece el suyo de vuelta. cómo el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol 2023 marcó a los peloteros latinos
Por qué los Dodgers siguen siendo los favoritos, con o sin esta duda
El talento sobrante es un buen problema. Muy pocas franquicias en la historia reciente de la MLB han podido decir que tienen demasiados buenos relevistas para una sola posición, y los Dodgers de 2026 están en ese punto. La profundidad del bullpen angelino no depende de resolver quién cierra; depende de que todas las piezas ejecuten cuando llegue octubre.
Díaz en roles de séptimo u octavo inning sigue siendo Díaz: su slider sigue siendo uno de sus pitcheos más difíciles de conectar, y su velocidad no ha caído a niveles preocupantes según los reportes de su llegada. [DATO PENDIENTE: velocidad promedio de Díaz en apariciones recientes o spring training 2026 para contrastar con pico de carrera.] El riesgo real no es el físico; es la cabeza. Los cerradores que pasan a roles de preparación tienden a rendir menos no porque les falte talento, sino porque les falta el disparador mental del noveno inning.
Los Dodgers han navegado tensiones de roster más complicadas que esta y han salido campeones. Si alguien puede gestionar el ego del bullpen, es esa organización. Pero Díaz no es un nombre cualquiera — es una figura, un personaje, una marca — y lo que pase con él en estas últimas semanas de temporada regular va a decir mucho sobre cómo Los Ángeles llega al postemporada.
- Edwin Díaz carrera y trayectoria en los Mets

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Edwin Díaz to return to Dodgers on Friday, but not as closer
item.dc:creator: Jack Baer
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers made Edwin Díaz the highest-paid reliever in MLB history last offseason. Their return so far has been an 11.85 ERA and two injured list stints. Díaz's season is set to resume Friday, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters Thursday morning before the team clinched its 13th National League West title in 14 years. When asked what role Díaz will occupy upon returning, Roberts had two words ready. "Low leverage." Instead of serving as closer, Díaz will be trying to earn a
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made Edwin Díaz the highest-paid reliever in MLB history last offseason. Their return so far has been an 11.85 ERA and two injured list stints.
Díaz's season is set to resume Friday, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters Thursday morning before the team clinched its 13th National League West title in 14 years. When asked what role Díaz will occupy upon returning, Roberts had two words ready.
"Low leverage."
Instead of serving as closer, Díaz will be trying to earn any sort of bullpen role as his team figures out its playoff roster. Roberts made clear that the Dodgers won't just be plugging him into the late innings this time around:
"I think like anything, it should be a meritocracy. You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also got to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we're at now, we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That's what he's about."
Díaz has appeared in only 16 games this season. He pitched for three weeks in March and April before hitting the IL with loose bodies in his throwing elbow, then returned in July with even more disastrous results. The Dodgers tried to stick with him as closer, but a stretch of 11 earned runs allowed in nine appearances ended with another trip to the IL on Aug. 18, this time with neck inflammation cited as the reason.
Díaz has been on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City since early September, but the results have been hardly encouraging. He walked seven batters and allowed six runs across five appearances.
His most recent appearance was a scoreless inning, though, with his lone baserunner coming on a two-out double from Miguel Andujar in a 12-0 win over the El Paso Chihuahuas.
That performance was apparently good enough for the Dodgers to decide he was ready for a return to the big leagues, with Roberts saying it was "really good" and "his best one yet."
As far as what the Dodgers are looking for when Díaz returns, Roberts said "Quality strike-throwing and get guys out."
With Díaz scuffling all season, Tanner Scott — who himself had a rough first season in 2025 after signing a big contract with the Dodgers — has primarily stepped in as closer and performed well enough, with a 2.87 ERA and 22 saves in 65 appearances. Amazingly, the Dodgers' current relief struggles are nothing compared to what the team went through last season before winning its second straight World Series.

item.title: [vanguardia.com.mx] Dodgers darán más miedo: dos pilares en ofensiva y defensiva se acercan al regreso
item.dc:creator: Pascual Escandón
item.description: Dodgers darán más miedo: dos pilares en ofensiva y defensiva se acercan al regreso Edwin Díaz será activado este viernes ante San Francisco, mientras Andy Pages está cerca de volver tras superar una fractura en la mano izquierda Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles afinan los últimos detalles de su roster mientras se preparan para la postemporada. Con el boleto a octubre ya asegurado, la organización trabaja en recuperar a dos elementos que pueden tener un papel importante: Edwin Díaz y Andy Pages. La sit
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers darán más miedo: dos pilares en ofensiva y defensiva se acercan al regreso
Edwin Díaz será activado este viernes ante San Francisco, mientras Andy Pages está cerca de volver tras superar una fractura en la mano izquierda
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles afinan los últimos detalles de su roster mientras se preparan para la postemporada. Con el boleto a octubre ya asegurado, la organización trabaja en recuperar a dos elementos que pueden tener un papel importante: Edwin Díaz y Andy Pages.
La situación de ambos es diferente. Díaz regresará este viernes para el inicio de la serie ante los Gigantes de San Francisco, aunque el mánager Dave Roberts adelantó que el relevista será utilizado inicialmente en situaciones de baja presión. Pages, por su parte, también se perfila para volver durante la actual estancia de los Dodgers en casa, pero todavía no tiene una fecha exacta de activación.
DÍAZ REGRESA, PERO TENDRÁ QUE RECUPERAR LA CONFIANZA
El regreso del puertorriqueño representa uno de los principales temas para el bullpen angelino. Díaz tiene efectividad de 11.85 en 16 apariciones, con 13.2 entradas lanzadas, 19 ponches y un WHIP de 2.56, números que explican la cautela del cuerpo técnico.
El escenario es muy diferente al que se esperaba cuando los Dodgers contrataron al tres veces All-Star durante el invierno para asumir el papel de cerrador.
Roberts ha sido directo al hablar de la situación del relevista y dejó claro que deberá demostrar nuevamente que puede ser una opción confiable en los momentos de mayor presión. Díaz no tiene garantizado recuperar inmediatamente el puesto de cerrador, especialmente con otros relevistas que han asumido responsabilidades importantes durante su ausencia.
La última salida de rehabilitación del boricua fue más alentadora: trabajó una entrada sin permitir carreras en Triple-A, antes de recibir la confirmación de que regresaría al equipo grande.
Sin embargo, sus actuaciones anteriores en las menores habían generado preocupación. Los Dodgers quieren verlo recuperar ritmo y control antes de volver a colocarlo en situaciones de alta exigencia.
PAGES, EL REFUERZO QUE NECESITA LA OFENSIVA
Mientras Díaz deberá reconstruir su lugar dentro del bullpen, Andy Pages representa una alternativa importante para fortalecer la alineación.
El cubano se encuentra en la lista de lesionados debido a una fractura en la mano izquierda y ha estado trabajando progresivamente en su swing. Los Dodgers planean activarlo durante la actual estancia en casa sin enviarlo a una asignación de rehabilitación en las ligas menores.
Antes de la lesión, Pages había establecido números importantes en su segunda temporada completa en Grandes Ligas. En 128 juegos bateó para .272, conectó 21 cuadrangulares, produjo 80 carreras, anotó 72 y robó 12 bases, además de registrar un OPS de .796.
Esos números convierten su regreso en una noticia relevante para una ofensiva que busca llegar completa a octubre.
La intención es que Pages vuelva a ocupar el jardín central, mientras Tommy Edman regresaría a la segunda base cuando el cubano esté disponible.
DOS REGRESOS CON OBJETIVOS MUY DISTINTOS
Los caminos de Díaz y Pages hacia la postemporada serán diferentes.
Díaz tendrá que demostrar que puede volver a ser una alternativa confiable para los innings de mayor presión, mientras que Pages buscará recuperar rápidamente el ritmo ofensivo que tenía antes de sufrir la fractura.
Para los Dodgers, ambos movimientos llegan en un momento particularmente importante. La organización ya consiguió el campeonato de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y aseguró su presencia en la postemporada, pero ahora debe definir qué jugadores llegarán en mejores condiciones al mes de octubre.
El regreso de Pages puede darle mayor profundidad al lineup, mientras que la recuperación de Díaz podría ampliar las alternativas de Roberts en el bullpen.
La serie contra San Francisco marcará el primer paso del regreso de Díaz, mientras Pages espera recibir el alta durante los próximos días. Los dos tendrán poco tiempo para demostrar que están listos para afrontar el escenario de mayor presión de la temporada.

La prime
item.content:encoded:
La tambaleante asignación de rehabilitación del puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz ha llegado a su fin.
Se espera que Díaz sea activado de la lista de lesionados el viernes en Los Ángeles, informó el manager Dave Roberts antes del juego del jueves en Cincinnati. Completó un inning en blanco en su quinta salida de rehabilitación con Triple-A Oklahoma City el miércoles, un paso hacia adelante luego de permitir cinco carreras limpias en dos tercios de entrada en su presentación anterior el domingo.
La primera temporada del contrato de tres años y US$69 millones de Díaz con los Dodgers ha estado llena de adversidades. Dos pasantías por la lista de lesionados — primero debido a una cirugía para remover cuerpos libres de su codo derecho en abril, y actualmente una inflamación en el cuello que lo marginó en agosto — lo han mantenido alejado de la lomita de Grandes Ligas durante la mayor parte de la campaña. Cuando ha estado sano, no ha rendido, registrando efectividad de 11.85 con cuatro salvamentos desperdiciados en 11 oportunidades.
Lee también: Miguel Rojas castigó a Cincinnati
Los Dodgers inicialmente esperaban que la asignación de rehabilitación de Díaz fuera breve, pero necesitaban ver más de él antes de activarlo de la lista de lesionados. En cinco oportunidades con Oklahoma City, Díaz permitió seis carreras en 4.1 entradas (efectividad de 12.46). Sus problemas de control han continuado, ya que otorgó más boletos (siete) que ponches (cuatro).
Tal como estaban las cosas, Díaz ya estaba destinado a ser utilizado en situaciones de menor apremio al regresar de la lista de lesionados. Pero también es posible que tenga que ganarse su lugar en el bullpen para la postemporada, ya que Roberts reconoció el lunes que podría quedar fuera del roster si no muestra avances.
“Creo que, como todo, debería ser una meritocracia”, señaló Roberts. “Tienes que ganarte el derecho a las oportunidades, pero luego también tienes que rendir, ¿verdad? Eddie entiende eso. Creo que en el punto en el que estamos ahora, necesitamos que los muchachos se comprometan, rindan y a partir de ahí veremos”.
Aquí tienes todo lo que debes saber sobre la última salida de rehabilitación de Díaz:
¿Cómo le fue?
Díaz realizó 15 pitcheos (11 strikes) para completar la novena entrada en blanco, sorteando un doblete con dos outs que salió del bate del dominicano Miguel Andújar, quien también se está rehabilitando, a 104.3 millas por hora. No indujo ningún swing en blanco en los ocho swings que hicieron en su contra (seis ante su slider y dos frente a su recta de cuatro costuras).
¿Qué están diciendo?
A pesar de que los números subyacentes detrás del inning en blanco de Díaz no fueron ideales, pudo trabajar con lo que tenía para conseguir tres outs — lo cual era lo que los Dodgers necesitaban ver de él.
“Calidad a la hora de lanzar strikes. Sacar outs. Probablemente sea eso”, indicó Roberts. “A medida que entras a la postemporada, cada entrada es de alto apremio”.
¿Qué sigue?
Los Dodgers vieron lo suficiente el miércoles como para traer de vuelta a Díaz para sus últimos nueve juegos de la temporada regular. Comenzará lanzando en situaciones de bajo apremio, pero podría ganarse oportunidades de mayor responsabilidad si rinde.
¿Qué más?
- Los Dodgers recibieron un refuerzo para el bullpen el miércoles, activando a Kris Bubic, adquisición de la Fecha Límite de Cambios, de la lista de lesionados de 60 días. El zurdo tiró un inning en blanco en su debut con el equipo para comenzar a presentar sus argumentos de cara al bullpen de postemporada de Los Ángeles.
- El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez mantiene las esperanzas de regresar para la postemporada luego de que unas imágenes de su espalda revelaran una distensión de bajo grado, informó Roberts. En medio de la incertidumbre con Díaz, Henríquez sería una opción para cerrar juegos en octubre si está sano.
- El cerrador de la postemporada del año pasado, Roki Sasaki, podría asumir un rol de similar este año una vez que sea activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días debido a una ampolla en el dedo medio derecho. Sin embargo, los Dodgers lo mantendrán como abridor por ahora mientras evalúan sus necesidades.
MLB.com.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
item.dc:creator: JEFF WALLNER
item.description: Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Rojos de Cincinnati. “Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos
item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Rojos de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki has been sidelined for the last three weeks due to a lingering blister. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki has been sidelined for the last three weeks due to a lingering blister.
After dealing with the blister during a late-August start, Sasaki was removed from the game and later added to the injured list.
"When I was facing the first hitter in the fourth inning, I actually didn't feel anything coming beforehand," Sasaki said through an interpreter after that game. "My skin just ripped off, and then after that, it got worse. ... I thought I was able to manage at first because the skin was still there, but after that, it kept getting worse, and I think it affected my slider afterwards."
As he has continued to recover and trend back towards the mound, Sasaki threw a simulated game on Wednesday, in which he completed four innings.
The Dodgers were thinking about having Sasaki pitch in Thursday's series finale against the Cincinnati Reds, but instead elected for the sim game, and to have him set up to return next week.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said on Wednesday. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. ... So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
At first, the Dodgers weren't sure if Sasaki would be back in the rotation — where he appeared for 23 starts this season — or if he would head to the bullpen.
However, after Blake Snell exited Wednesday's start after one inning, Roberts confirmed Sasaki would rejoin the rotation for the time being.
Sasaki had a 4.72 ERA across the first eight starts of his MLB career last season before he was placed on the injured list with a shoulder impingement for over four months. Upon his late-September return, he was not placed back into the rotation, but rather into a bullpen role that saw plenty of success.
In his first two innings of work, Sasaki struck out four and allowed just one hit and zero runs. His next appearance came in the postseason.
For the remainder of the postseason — one that included the first three saves of his MLB career, the pivotal 8th through 10th innings of an NLDS thriller and even 2.2 innings in the World Series — Sasaki established a 0.84 ERA across 10.2 innings of work.
Sasaki will likely return to the bullpen for the postseason this year, especially with the question marks surrounding Edwin Díaz. However, for now, he appears set to make one more start, and improve upon his 4.60 ERA over 119.1 innings this season.

CINCINNATI -- The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons, sparked by four hits f
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers clinch 5th straight NL West title, 13th in 14 years, Tucker has 4 hits in 8-2 win over Reds
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons, sparked by four hits from Kyle Tucker that included a first-inning home run in an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, The two-time World Series ch...
CINCINNATI -- The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons, sparked by four hits from Kyle Tucker that included a first-inning home run in an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday,
The two-time World Series champions already were assured of their 14th straight postseason appearance, trying the record Atlanta set from 1991 to 2005. Los Angeles (93-60) had clinched no worse than a wild-card berth on Monday.
Los Angeles opened a 9 1/2-game lead over second-place San Diego and has the second-best record in the NL as they try to overtake Milwaukee (95-57 entering Thursday) for the top NL seed. The division clinching was the fourth earliest for the Dodgers after Sept. 10 in 2019, Sept. 13 in 2022 and Sept. 16 in 2023.
Tucker fell a triple short of the cycle and had three RBIs, hitting a single and a pair of doubles. He hit his 16th homer, a two-run drive in the first off Brady Singer, who allowed seven runs, nine hits and four walks in 3 1/3 innings.
Freddie Freeman's sacrifice fly and Tucker's RBI double boosted the lead in the second, and the Dodgers opened a 7-0 lead in the fourth on Max Muncy's two-run double and Josue De Paula's RBI single.
Dodger left-hander Justin Wrobleski, making his 22nd start this season and first since Sept. 6, did not allow a baserunner in three innings while striking out three.
Wrobleski and Blake Treinen combined to retire their first 11 batters before Sal Stewart's 32nd homer.
Landon Knack (1-0) allowed four hits over four scoreless innings for his first big league win since May 31 last year.
Miguel Rojas homered off Brandon Williamson in the ninth.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said reliever Edwin Díaz (neck inflammation) finished his minor league injury rehabilitation assignment and will be activated this weekend.
Dodgers: RHP Tyler Glasnow (4-1, 3.50) starts Friday against San Francisco, who send LHP Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.68) to the mound,
Reds: RHP Chase Burns (15-3, 2.80) starts Friday against the Chicago Cubs.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers, like all other 29 MLB teams, have around 10 games left on the schedule.
LA already knows it will be headed to October, but the Dodgers are still aiming to clinch the NL West, which could happen on Thursday afternoon.
As the Dodgers gear up for October, one of the biggest storylines surrounding the team is who will close games out.
Edwin Diaz was signed to be the team's closer, but he's had inconsistency problems. On Thursday, during their series with the Reds, LA revealed its plans with Edwin Diaz.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Dealt Positive Shohei Ohtani News During Reds Series
Edwin Diaz to be Activated Off IL on Friday
According to multiple reporters who follow the Los Angeles Dodgers, Edwin Diaz will be activated from the Injured List on Friday.
"Dave Roberts said Edwin Diaz will meet team in Los Angeles. When he is activated it will be "low leverage" situations and will have to earn higher leverage spots."
So, that basically rules out the possibility that Edwin Diaz will be a closer for the Dodgers, which is a good call by Dave Roberts. Despite a few solid outings on paper, it feels like every time Diaz has pitched for the Dodgers this season, there's always been added nerves to the situation.
More MLB on Heavy: Blake Snell's Latest Injury Comments Should Not Faze Los Angeles Dodgers Fans
More on Edwin Diaz Injury….
Edwin Diaz has been sidelined since mid-August with a neck injury.
He will be eased into the bullpen fold, and the good news for LA is that they may have already wrapped up the NL West when Diaz joins the team in LA on Friday.
"Díaz signed a three-year, $69MM contract over the winter, but it's been a lost season for the All-Star closer. He's pitched in just 13 2/3 big league innings due to injury and hasn't looked anywhere close to his usual self when healthy enough to take the mound. He's been rocked for 18 runs on 25 hits and 10 walks, leading to an awful 11.85 earned run average. Díaz entered the season with a career 39.9% strikeout rate and 8.6% walk rate. Those marks have plummeted to 24.1% and 12.7% this season, and his average fastball has dropped from 97.2 mph in 2025 to 96.3 mph in 2026."
In other Dodgers news, Andy Pages could be nearing a return as well, and manager Dave Roberts did not rule out a return for Shohei Ohtani during the regular season, which has just a week and a half left.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: No more bubbly — NL West champion Dodgers appear headed for early fall
item.dc:creator: Bill Plaschke

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
They hit their magic number, but minus the magic.
The Dodgers trudged toward October by clinching their 13th National League West title in 14 years on Thursday, their customary march mired in a quicksand of questions.
Has any Dodger team during this golden era entered the playoffs with more injuries, more uncertainty, and a greater fear of underachievement?
Will the party in Cincinnati be the last time they celebrate this season?
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
The Three-Peat looks like a no-go.
Despite the best efforts from baseball’s best braintrust, their latest creation simply doesn’t have the appearance of a championship team.
They’re aging, they’re hurting and, with only a couple of weeks left until the beginning of their annual autumnal angst, they look tired and taut and unprepared for this monumental tussle with history.
“I think for me, the message was, ‘We haven’t come close to playing our best baseball yet.’” manager Dave Roberts told reporters when relaying his speech to the team earlier this week upon clinching a record-tying 14th consecutive playoff berth.
He added, “The message was, we’ve accomplished a lot up to this point, all the while not playing our best baseball. So let’s get some of these guys healthy.”
Haven’t come close to playing our best baseball… Let’s get some of these guys healthy.
Not exactly “Win one for the Gipper” stuff, but completely accurate. These postseason’s themes are more realistic than inspirational, and for good reason.
No, they haven’t come close to playing their best baseball. Forget what you see in these season-ending games against some of the worst teams. Remember, instead, what they’ve done against some of baseball’s best.
Since the All-Star break, they are 4-12 against the five National League playoff contenders. The Atlanta Braves swept them. The Chicago Cubs swept them. The Milwaukee Brewers dominated them.
These teams will be waiting for them in October, and even baseball’s richest roster might not be enough to carry this staggered bunch through their toughest stretch. They’ve played a lot of games in three years, all under baseball’s brightest spotlight, every night, scores of media, millions of fans, a worldwide whirl for 28 regular dudes, and it’s finally taken its toll.
They’ve hit the wall… and the wall is about to hit back.
“It’s not easy, I think it’s a lot harder than people think it is,” said Roberts. “Human nature alone, when you’re hungry, when you’re chasing something, it’s a lot more easy to be motivated, versus, having been there, done that, it gets a little trite, a little old.”
He added: “To keep guys enthusiastic, focused, hungry, that’s harder. But to their credit, they stayed the course. And for me, we’re just as hungry as we were in ‘24 and ‘25. This is a separate season. Our guys understand.”
The 1988-89 Lakers understood, too. And they still got burned in ways that Dodger fans will find painfully familiar. Showtime was chasing the original “three-peat” trademarked by Pat Riley when the Lakers were swept by the Detroit Pistons in a Finals that seemed cursed,
Byron Scott missed the series with a hamstring injury and Magic Johnson essentially missed the final two games with a hamstring injury and they couldn’t survive.
This looks like the Dodgers today. Their injuries feel too major, and the impact too deep.
Start with Shohei Ohtani. The Dodgers haven’t won a full-season championship in 38 years without him at the top of the lineup. He’ll be there again, but his body has been breaking down for the last couple of months, and, before being recently placed on the injured list — finally! — he was only a shadow of himself.
He hasn’t hit a home run or driven in a run outside of Coors Field in more than a month. In his last 24 games before going on the IL with biceps and knee issues, he was batting .198. The Dodgers can’t admit it, and Ohtani would never acknowledge it, but this is a man in serious need of an extended rest.
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
Also on the injured list in these final days is Andy Pages, who was having a career year before breaking his hand. He’ll return without much time to get ready for October, and this is a man who will need some time, as he has a career .114 average in the postseason and was even benched last year before he redeemed himself with that picturesque catch over Kiké Hernández.
Speaking of last October’s heroes, the biggest savior has also spent the summer in pain, Will Smith battling neck issues until recently returning to the lineup. But the comeback has been bumpy. In his initial games since returning at the start of September, Smith was batting .171. Last October he set a major league record by catching 73 innings in the World Series. He is still paying the price.
Then there’s Freddie Freeman, whose bat doesn’t have the same pop, who’s step doesn’t have the same spring, and who has his worst OPS in 14 years. Add an inconsistent Mookie Betts and an incredibly streaky Teoscar Hernández to an already-shaky lineup.
It’s been such an unsteady year, Andrew Friedman’s two big offseason acquisitions have been busts. Edwin Díaz has been terrible, and then injured, then terrible again. Kyle Tucker has been terrible, then worse, then mostly invisible.
Even the Dodgers two role-playing heroes have seemingly disappeared. Kiké Hernández, at age 35, has his lowest home-run total — three — in 12 years. Miguel Rojas, at age 37, has his lowest home run and RBI totals in nine years.
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
As if they didn’t have enough problems on the field and at the plate, check out the mound. No, don’t.
Even what should be their strength is now being threatened. Blake Snell left Wednesday’s game early with groin issues and Tyler Glasnow recently complained of general discomfort. This leaves a proven playoff rotation of two, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal, and if you think Yamamoto threw a lot of innings last October, this time he won’t be able to leave the mound for a month.
In all, this is a Dodger team facing its toughest challenge yet, their quest for an historic three-peat much tougher than the last two journeys, one that will require arguably the greatest stretch of baseball in franchise history to complete.
This division title is a nice beginning.
It could also be the end.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dave Roberts can't hide Dodgers' issues with Shohei Ohtani, Edwin Diaz updates
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers may be back to their winning ways, but it's impossible for fans to ignore the fact that they've been playing sub-.500 teams since the beginning of September and only have one series against a winning team left on their schedule. The rotation has been hit with another injury, the bullpen is still in bad shape, Shohei Ohtani is still injured and, maybe worst of all, Edwin Díaz is coming back. Dave Roberts said ahead of the Dodgers' finale against the Cincinnati Reds that Dí
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers may be back to their winning ways, but it's impossible for fans to ignore the fact that they've been playing sub-.500 teams since the beginning of September and only have one series against a winning team left on their schedule.
The rotation has been hit with another injury, the bullpen is still in bad shape, Shohei Ohtani is still injured and, maybe worst of all, Edwin Díaz is coming back.
Dave Roberts said ahead of the Dodgers' finale against the Cincinnati Reds that Díaz will be activated on Friday, but with the caveat that he'll only pitch in low leverage. Of Ohtani: "He's feeling normal...ish" but continues to progress. Neither are ringing endorsements.
Dodgers fans have been forced to wonder if any lead would be too big for Díaz to blow. He bounced back from a disastrous rehab appearance (⅔ innings, five earned runs) with a much more promising one (one scoreless), but the Díaz conundrum is one they're going to have to go back to the drawing board with in the offseason.
Ohtani is eligible to come off the IL next Wednesday and the Dodgers will want to give him a ramp-up before the postseason, but "normal...ish" is not an indication that they should.
Edwin Díaz set to return to Dodgers on Friday; Shohei Ohtani feeling "normal...ish"
The Dodgers are still trying to lock up a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves, who are only behind by 3.5 games, so they still can't just rest on their laurels after clinching the NL West. Using Díaz in any of the games ahead, even if it's a 10-plus run blowout, doesn't seem wise.
But they also can't just ignore their $69 million closer entirely. What we might see from the Dodgers is a soft ghosting — maybe Díaz will only get the ball in a favorable matchup to end an inning. Under no circumstances should he be allowed on LA's postseason roster.
When it comes to Ohtani, the situation gets even more sticky. He'll presumably take back his leadoff spot in the Dodgers' lineup when he returns, but if he looks anything like he did in his last game before going onto the IL, postseason opponents will be more than happy to take the easy out to start a game.
Don't let the Dodgers' postseason berth and clinching the NL West fool you: they're in some trouble. Their 2024 and 2025 postseason rosters all had their own weaknesses, but this year's might be the most jeopardized we've seen yet.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– Edwin Díaz is set to be activated by the Dodgers on Friday, manager Dave Roberts announced.
It leaves the $69 million offseason signing with plenty to prove over the final week of the regular season.
After beginning the year as a marquee free-agent acquisition seen as one of the best closers in all the major leagues, Díaz’s first season in Los Angeles has been an injury-plagued, performance-hampered disaster.
He has made only 16 appearances. He has converted only seven of his 11 save opportunities. He has posted an unthinkable 11.85 ERA while dealing with a litany of physical ailments.
First, there were loose bodies in his elbow that required a surgical procedure in April. Then, after returning in late July, he went down again with neck inflammation just three weeks later. At other points, he complained of discomfort in his previously surgically repaired right knee. Put it all together, he has never looked right with his mechanics or delivery.
The Dodgers were hopeful Díaz’s latest IL stint would give him time to remedy those issues. They identified a drop in his arm slot as a potential root cause for his lack of consistency this year.
But then, in his first four rehab outings with Triple-A Oklahoma City earlier this month, he gave up six runs (including five in one appearance) and walked seven batters, prompting Roberts earlier this week to cast doubt on Díaz’s chances of making the postseason roster.
“He needs to pitch better,” Roberts said. “It hasn’t been good.”
On Wednesday, at least, Díaz seemed to get the message. He retired three of the four batters he faced in another rehab outing. And while he didn’t record a swing-and-miss, he also didn’t issue a walk.
“Really good,” Roberts said. “It was his best one yet.”
Thus, the Dodgers feel comfortable bringing the 32-year-old back to the big leagues now.
He will start in lower-leverage situations, according to Roberts said, and will need to show further progress to regain the club’s trust.
“I think like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also got to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now, we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
As for what he’ll need to show to revive his chances of pitching in October?
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said simply. “As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it.”

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Will Shohei Ohtani return from injury before MLB playoffs? Here's the latest update appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are vying for their third consecutive World Series title. And of course, everyone is wondering about Shohei Ohtani.
He has been battling a series of injuries, including knee inflammation, bicep tightness, and neck strain.
On Thursday, manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani has been making progress, per Jack Harris of The California Post. He said that Ohtani will be making his way back to coach pitching.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Meanwhile, Roberts said that Ohtani is feeling "normalish," per Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic.
The Dodgers clinched their 14th straight playoff berth and are on track to win yet another National League West Division title. Los Angeles is a heavy favorite going into the postseason.
But for Ohtani, it's been an up-and-down year, especially on the mound.
Altogether, he has pitched in 14 games, posting an 8-2 record, a 1.79 ERA, and 95 strikeouts. However, injuries have kept Ohtani out of the starting rotation.
That has jeopardized his chances of winning another NL MVP Award. An honor that will likely go to Chicago Cubs CF Pete Crow-Armstrong. The contest between the two for the honor has captivated the baseball world in the later half of the season.
Nevertheless, Ohtani has remained solid at the plate, even as his numbers declined. He is batting .277 with 139 hits, 30 home runs, and 80 RBIs.
In his NL MVP season last year, Ohtani batted .282 with 172 hits, 55 home runs, and 102 RBIs.
The Dodgers will wrap up a road series against the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday. Afterward, they will begin a home series against the San Francisco Giants.
Related: Dodgers' Dave Roberts shares important Andy Pages, Edwin Diaz injury updates
Related: Dodgers promote pitcher after making Bobby Miller roster move

item.title: [Orange County Register] Dave Roberts: First-round bye would be more ‘beneficial’ than ever for injury-riddled Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: CINCINNATI — A few days off sounds pretty good right about now. “I do think this team, as much as any team we’ve had, that week off is probably most beneficial,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of locking down one of the top two seeds in the National League in order to get a first-round bye and five days off before starting the postseason. Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch th
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — A few days off sounds pretty good right about now.
“I do think this team, as much as any team we’ve had, that week off is probably most beneficial,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of locking down one of the top two seeds in the National League in order to get a first-round bye and five days off before starting the postseason.
Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch that first-round bye. The Dodgers trail the Milwaukee Brewers by three games for the top seed.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset,” Roberts said. “But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge.”
Blake Snell joined the long list of players with injury concerns when he left his start Wednesday after just one inning due to left groin tightness. The Dodgers also have questions about Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps), Freddie Freeman (knee), Edgardo Henriquez (back), Andy Pages (hand), Roki Sasaki (blister) and Dalton Rushing (elbow).
Pages has been swinging a bat and hitting off the Trajekt machine this week, and it is “very likely” he will be activated from the IL during the homestand starting Friday, according to Roberts.
Ohtani has been “progressing” this week and is feeling “normal-ish” with no pain in his right arm or left knee, Roberts said.
“He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when (his) time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Snell could undergo an MRI to determine the severity of his groin injury. But he was optimistic after the game Wednesday that he had pulled back and left the game soon enough that it won’t be a serious issue and he might be able to make one more start before the end of the regular season.
“It’s all contingent on how he feels and potential imaging,” Roberts said. “It doesn’t make sense to just shut him down until the postseason if he can pitch. But again, if he’s not 100 percent to pitch, then we have no problem kicking the can.”
DIAZ RETURN
Right-hander Edwin Diaz completed his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday and will join the Dodgers in Los Angeles this weekend with the expectation that he will be activated from the Injured List.
Diaz will be used in “low-leverage” situations, Roberts said, with a need to prove he can pitch well enough to assume a bigger role if he is on the postseason roster.
“I think, like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also have to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Roberts called Diaz’s final outing with OKC was “his best one yet.” Diaz pitched a scoreless inning, gave up a double and didn’t get a single swing-and-miss on any of 15 pitches.
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said of what he hopes to see from Diaz. “That’s probably it. As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it. Quality of strike-throwing, and get guys out.”
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Cesar Perdomo, 0-1, 3.68 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 4-1, 3.50 ERA), Friday, 7:10 p.m., Apple TV, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
Edwin Díaz se unirá este viernes a los Dodgers en el inicio de una serie ante los Giants de San Francisco. (Nick Wass)
Por Redacción El Nuevo Día
El relevista puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz retornará con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles cuando la novena lo active de la lista de lesionados este viernes, confirmó el dirigente Dave Roberts.
El regreso de Díaz se producirá después de completar el miércoles una entrada sin permitir carreras en su quinta aparición de rehabilitación en Triple A con la novena de Oklahoma City.
“La idea es que esté activo el viernes”, expresó Roberts este jueves, según SportsNet LA.
El naguabeño trabajó la novena entrada y necesitó 15 lanzamientos, 11 de ellos para strikes. Permitió un doble con dos outs, pero evitó que el corredor anotara para completar el episodio en blanco.
Roberts calificó la actuación como la mejor de Díaz durante su asignación de rehabilitación.
Dodgers injury updates, per manager Roberts (via @ByJackHarris):
• Edwin Diaz (neck) will be activated from IL on Friday • Andy Pages (hand) "very likely" to be activated during final homestand • Shohei Ohtani (biceps) could still return before end of regular season
La salida resultaba particularmente importante para el boricua después de su difícil presentación del domingo, cuando permitió cinco carreras limpias, concedió tres bases por bolas y apenas consiguió dos outs.
De hecho, Roberts había reconocido el lunes que Díaz necesitaba lanzar mejor y que su presencia en el roster de los Dodgers para la postemporada no estaba garantizada.
El regreso tampoco significa que Díaz retomará inmediatamente las funciones de cerrador.
Roberts había adelantado que utilizará inicialmente al derecho de 32 años en situaciones de poca presión mientras intenta recuperar la confianza del cuerpo técnico.
Los Dodgers ya aseguraron su pase a los playoffs y marchan primeros en la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. El viernes inician una serie de tres juegos ante San Francisco.
Díaz está en la lista de lesionados desde el 18 de agosto debido a una inflamación en el cuello. Es su segunda ausencia prolongada de la temporada luego de que en abril fuera sometido a una operación para remover cuerpos sueltos de su codo derecho.
Díaz tiene marca de 2-2 y efectividad de 11.85 en 16 apariciones, con 18 carreras limpias permitidas en 13.2 entradas. Además, ha desperdiciado cuatro de sus 11 oportunidades de salvamento.

item.content:encoded:
This is your one-stop shop for every Dodgers stint on the injured list during the 2026 season. We’ll also include every time a player misses time on the paternity list, bereavement leave, or is on the family medical emergency list as well.
Basically any time a player misses time that requires a roster move, we’ll note it here.
During the 2025 season, 28 different Dodgers players spent time on the injured list, some of them for multiple stints. That matched the team total from 2024, while in 2023 the Dodgers saw 34 players miss time on the IL.
Every injured-list stint is a transaction and will also be chronicled on our 40-man roster page. Both are essentially living documents that will be constantly updated throughout the season as these moves happen.
Injured-list stints for pitchers are a minimum of 15 days, and for position players it’s at least 10 days.
During spring training, the Dodgers placed both Evan Phillips and Kiké Hernández on the 60-day injured list, which opened up space on the 40-man roster for other moves. On opening day, six more Dodgers were placed on the injured list, including Blake Snell and Tommy Edman.

item.content:encoded:
The closer will be active for Game 1 of the Dodgers' series against the San Francisco Giants, manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Thursday.
Roberts added that Diaz will pitch in low-leverage situations.
The 32-year-old right-hander signed a three-year, $60-million contract in the off-season to become the Dodgers' closer, but has struggled with injuries and underperformance.
Diaz underwent an arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right eblow in April and most recently missed time due to neck inflammation. He has an 11.85 ERA with 19 strikeouts and 10 walks over 13.2 innings.
Roberts also said that the Dodgers plan to activate outfielder Andy Pages on their upcoming homestand, and that Shohei Ohtani could still return this season.
The two-time reigning National League MVP tried to return from a nagging bicep injury on Sept. 7 but was placed on the 15-day injured list afterward. He will not pitch again this season.
